test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A rectangular sheet measures 40 { cm} in length and 25 { cm} in width. A right-angled triangle with base 12 { cm} and height 8 { cm} is cut off from one corner of the rectangle. Find the area of the remaining sheet.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining Area = (Total Rectangle Area) − (Area of the Cut-off Triangle)

Total Rectangle Area = 40 × 25 = 1000 cm²

Area of Right-angled Triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 12 × 8 = 48 cm²

Remaining Area = 1000 − 48 = 952 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 952 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the rectangular sheet (L) = 40 cm

Width of the rectangular sheet (W) = 25 cm

Base of the right-angled triangle (b) = 12 cm

Height of the right-angled triangle (h) = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of Rectangle = Length × Width

Area of Right-angled Triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6308a7367dd389e6a7194893aad1ad67161cbb165150e729bc263642725a452.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total area of the sheet = 40 × 25

⇒ Total area = 1000 cm²

⇒ Area of the triangle removed = 1/2 × 12 × 8

⇒ Area of the triangle removed = 6 × 8 = 48 cm²

⇒ Area of the remaining sheet = Total area − Area of removed triangle

⇒ Area of the remaining sheet = 1000 − 48

⇒ Area of the remaining sheet = 952 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 952 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Triangle

For any triangle with base (b) and height (h), Area = 1/2 × b × h. If three sides a, b, c are given, use Heron's formula: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s = (a+b+c)/2.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse (k) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: k² = b² + h².

Area of Composite Figures

The area of a composite figure can be found by adding the areas of its simpler parts or by subtracting the area of a removed part from the total area.
